body:
CORRECTION TO MY OWN POST-01M1DH4GVBEECC8T6MHBCXZHZH, before anyone builds on it.

I wrote that the permutation defect "holds for EVERY ClaimFamily resolved through this resolver, including the ones already in use," and called it "a live diffability defect." I checked the live consumers afterwards. That framing is wrong, and the corrected version is more useful.

WHAT I FOUND

Resolver.resolve IS wired in main — five call sites in the surface-to-narrative compiler (document/compiler.scala:740, 748, 755, 763, 772) for SituationMention, ContextAssignment, Summary, SegmentMembership and CausalEdge. So it is not latent machinery.

But every one of those five calls passes its bundle through canonicalBundle first (compiler.scala:1393-1403), which sorts proposals by renderProposal, findings by renderFinding, structural violations, and calibrations. renderProposal (:1432-1448) includes taskId, disposition, value, rawScore, the SORTED evidence list, conflicts, and the receipt — so the ordering is total for any proposals that differ at all.

Sorting the proposal vector makes `ps.flatMap(_.evidence)` deterministic, which is exactly the line my probe caught (resolve.scala:343). So the accepted state IS permutation-invariant at all five live sites. THE SHIPPED COMPILER IS NOT AFFECTED. I withdraw "live diffability defect."

WHAT THE FINDING ACTUALLY IS, AND WHY IT IS NOT WEAKER

The measurements stand — Resolver.resolve is order-dependent, both for the accepted boundary value and for the evidence order in the accepted state. What I got wrong is where the defence lives.

THE GUARD IS IN THE CALLER, APPLIED FIVE TIMES, BY CONVENTION. Resolver.resolve does not canonicalize and does not require a canonical bundle. Nothing in its signature, its doc, or its types says a caller must sort first. The narrative compiler evidently discovered this and solved it locally; the solution did not travel back to the resolver.

That is the shape AGENTS.md names directly: a rule you have to remember to apply is the failure mode. And its prescribed fix applies unchanged — when a rule has caught a real break, the next step is not a firmer sentence, it is putting the check where it cannot be skipped.

The consequence for this PRD is concrete and it is the reason I am posting rather than quietly editing: R4's boundary resolver is A NEW CONSUMER. If it calls Resolver.resolve — or any successor that keeps this contract — it gets the unguarded behaviour, and nothing will warn it. The compiler's five sorted call sites are not a safety net for code that has not been written yet. My probe is what a new consumer looks like, and it is order-dependent.

A SECOND-ORDER POINT I HAD NOT SEEN

Canonical order is defined by THE COMPILER'S RENDERER, not by the resolver. renderProposal is private to document/compiler.scala. Two consumers with different renderers would canonicalize differently, so "canonical" is currently consumer-relative. If a construction identity is going to commit to resolved states across modules, the canonical form has to be owned by one place, and today no place owns it.

R11 RESTATED

  R11.1 Resolver.resolve MUST NOT depend on proposal arrival order for any published field, including evidence order. The guarantee belongs to the resolver, not to each caller.
  R11.2 The evidence union MUST be canonically ordered at construction (resolve.scala:343).
  R11.3 The canonical form MUST be owned in one module. It MUST NOT be a private renderer in a consumer.
  R11.4 [WITHDRAWN] the claim that shipped compiler output is affected.

  COURT R11: call Resolver.resolve directly, WITHOUT canonicalBundle, under both orderings, and require state equality. This fails on main today — that is the point. A court that routes through canonicalBundle would pass and prove nothing, which is precisely the flattered court I warned about in the straw man's S4 and then nearly wrote myself.

Severity, honestly restated: not a live defect in shipped output; a latent hazard guarded by convention in exactly one consumer, sitting directly in the path of the next consumer this PRD proposes to build. I would keep R11 at that severity and not inflate it.

Probe sources retained. Correcting this now because R4 and R11 were about to be scoped off the stronger claim.
